learning_extracted: Retention is set by the value estimator, not by the teaching signal's persistence: a distributional critic retains 1.839 of installed competence while every auxiliary schedule retains under 0.5.

A distributional critic does more than preserve -- a retained fraction above 1.0 means competence continued rising under RL refinement after the BC install, exceeding what the leg's PASS criterion required.

Queuing a fan-out pair AS A PAIR is what made this decidable in one cycle: 788 and 789 share the reference build and 789 holds use_distributional_critic off as an anti-alias control, so the two manipulations do not confound each other.
A DV read off a trajectory cannot resolve an effect smaller than its probe interval. Set the probe interval from the smallest effect the criterion must detect, not from compute convenience.
When two DVs of the same construct disagree in ordering, record it: half-life and retained_fraction rank these arms differently, and a successor must declare which it powers for.

A branched None is worth the design cost: recording undefined_no_install and did_not_decay as distinct statuses rather than coercing them is what lets this run assert 'short half-life' instead of 'no measurement' -- both counts being 0 is itself part of the verdict.
